overall_notes: The engineering scaffolding is well ahead of the product's data. Strict TypeScript builds clean, 1,088 tests pass, CI, deploy gates, backups and a yield canary all exist. Accessibility basics are solid, and the save/calendar/share layer works. What a user or AI system actually meets is less reliable. About 20% of listed events carry a phantom next-year date: the music-gig parser at scripts/scrape-all.ts:655 rolls past dates forward with no window, and these false dates appear in JSON-LD on the live site. About 40% of listed events show a venue-default price as if it were fact, and every Megaron event carries an invented 20:30. The raw marker '<!-- timeliness-expires -->' is visible on 343 pages. Coverage is thin: 5 events tonight, 4 exhibitions, and more.com is capped at 20 items per category. The measurement focus in INTENT is still mostly empty: citations and crawlers are null, and kpi.db tables have 0 rows. Highest-leverage fixes: (1) window the gig-date rollover and quarantine the ~185 rolled rows. This lifts accuracy, citability and search at once. (2) Stop rendering and emitting venue_default prices, defaulted times and unknown availability. Add a post-build dist scan for artifacts: comments, pipes, '&', missing og images, phantom dates. (3) Remove the more.com cap and batch-verify the top unverified Athens venues to roughly double real inventory. All scores are against the local build (ahead of live). Live spot checks show the same date and comment defects.
